correctness.rationale: PASS. Ultrahomogeneity of the Fraisse limit reduces injective ordered-tuple orbits to label-preserving isomorphism types of their finitely generated meet-substructures, and the generated substructure is exactly meet-closure. A finite meet-tree has a rooted-tree cover graph. Coloring tuple entries black and other generated points white produces a Greg tree because any white generated point must be the meet of black descendants from at least two distinct child subtrees. Conversely, in any rooted Greg tree every child subtree of a white vertex contains a black descendant (white leaves are forbidden), so the white vertex is the meet of black descendants chosen in two children; hence the whole meet-tree is generated by its black vertices. This gives the all-n bijection. The root species decomposition yields G=x exp(G)+(exp(G)-1-G), equivalently (1+x)exp(G)=1+2G and the stated Lambert-W branch. Equality partitions of coordinates give b_n=sum S(n,k)a_k and EGF G(e^x-1). Finite enumeration/coefficient checks are corroborative only.
risks: The result is for the universal homogeneous meet-tree in the language {<, meet}; expansions or reducts can have different orbit profiles.

originality.rationale: PASS. OEIS A005264 exactly contains the numerical Greg-tree sequence, white-vertex definition, EGF equation, and Lambert-W expression, so none of that enumeration is claimed new. Mennuni's full primary HTML states that finite meet-trees form a Fraisse class with universal homogeneous countable limit and that definable closure of a set is closure under meets; the Kaplan--Rzepecki--Siniora primary abstract studies generic automorphisms, not an orbit profile. The originality is the model-theoretic identification of injective tuple orbits with A005264 and the resulting repeated-coordinate Stirling transform. Resultary searches for universal homogeneous meet-tree + Greg/orbit profile returned no direct covering record, while exact database inspection confirms the combinatorial side is prior.
